back: Organisation owned by many governments providing finance, advice and technical help across borders.
Lends long-term at low interest for development projects; gives advice and research.
Promotes stable exchange rates and payments; lends for balance of payments problems; monitors economies.

front: Origin of the World Bank and IMF
back: Founded at the Bretton Woods conference, 1944.
Owned by countries of a region; finances infrastructure, enterprise and regional trade (e.g. the African Development Bank).
Conditions attached to a loan, such as policy reforms or spending cuts.
World Bank: long-term development projects. IMF: short-term balance of payments support and surveillance.
Benefits: finance, low interest, expertise, crisis support. Criticisms: debt, conditions, unsuitable policies, rich-country voting power.
